question_text: Integer keys are inserted, in this order, into an empty hash table with 7 slots (indexes 0 to 6), using the hashing function h(k) = k mod 7: 15, 22, 8, 29, 3. (i) Using linear probing, state the index at which each key is stored. (ii) Calculate the load factor after all five insertions. (iii) Instead, using separate chaining, state the contents of each non-empty slot. (iv) Explain why many implementations enlarge the table when the load factor exceeds a threshold such as 0.7.
